schedulerPaused.description: Global pause of the scheduler, preserved across restarts.

theme.description: Appearance of the interface. "system" follows the macOS setting and switches with it, sunset included.

engine.description: Which engine this application drives. Embedded is the default and the whole desktop install: the scheduler runs inside the application. Remote points it at a rotad — on this machine or another — and the application then draws an engine it does not own. One configuration directory must never be opened by two engines at once; the embedded one takes a lock on it, which is exactly what stops an application and a daemon from scheduling the same jobs twice.

mode.description: embedded runs the scheduler in this process; remote drives a rotad over HTTP.

url.description: Where the daemon answers, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:47823. Only read in remote mode.

token.description: Bearer token of that daemon. ${VARIABLE} is resolved from the .env file. Only read in remote mode.

bunPath.description: Explicit path to the bun binary. null = automatic resolution.

dockerPath.description: Explicit path to the docker binary, for sandboxed jobs. null = automatic resolution.

integrations.description: Destinations shared by all jobs. An address declared here is declared once and for all, rather than copied into every definition — and it does not follow job files when they are shared.

discordWebhookUrl.description: Outgoing webhook, enough to publish reports without creating a bot. Accepts ${VARIABLE}, resolved from the environment or the .env file: a webhook URL is worth a password. Failing that, the bot below can write too.

discordBotToken.description: Token of a Discord bot. Required to control Rota from a channel: a webhook can only write. Accepts ${VARIABLE}.

discordChannelId.description: Identifier of the channel where the bot accepts commands, and where it answers. This is the only access control: anyone who writes in that channel controls Rota. Direct messages are ignored.

discordControlEnabled.description: Allows control from Discord. Without this flag the bot does not connect — pasting a token is not enough to open a remote control onto your machine.

discordChatEnabled.description: Allows the `chat` command, which sends a message written in the channel to the agent of a job. A flag of its own because it is not the same power as `run`: run executes the prompt the job carries, chat lets anyone in the channel compose one. Requires control to be enabled.

mirrorReportsToDiscord.description: An agent's report tool also publishes to Discord, on top of opening its window. No effect until a destination is configured.

http.description: Local HTTP server. Three flags that stack on purpose: the first opens the port, the second exposes the API — which drives everything — and the third the webhook endpoint, which only starts jobs declaring a webhook trigger. Separating them lets a third-party service be given a webhook address without being given the rest.

enabled.description: Opens the port. Nothing is served until one of the two flags below is on as well, and nothing at all without a token.

listen.description: Listening address. 127.0.0.1 keeps the server on this machine; 0.0.0.0 makes it reachable from the network, which a webhook coming from outside needs — and past loopback, the token is the only thing between the network and this machine.

port.description: Listening port. The default is nothing well-known on purpose: a common port would already be taken, or worse, would answer in place of what you meant to reach.

token.description: Token expected in "Authorization: Bearer <token>", or in the X-Rota-Token header. Required to start the server, loopback included: without it, anything running locally could drive Rota — a web page in an open tab included. Accepts ${VARIABLE}.

apiEnabled.description: Exposes /api: list, run, stop, enable, history, logs, and chat with an agent. This is remote control of the machine — a job runs shell or an agent.

webhookEnabled.description: Exposes POST /webhook/<id>, which starts a job — and only a job that declares a webhook trigger. A job may carry a token of its own, so that the address handed out starts that job and nothing else.

defaults.description: Values applied to jobs that do not specify them.

inlineOutputBytes.description: Beyond this size, the output goes to a separate file instead of the JSONL.
